response.evidence: In this dataset of 2,000 loan decisions, Hispanic or Latino White females aged 35-44 show a 98.2% loan approval rate (56 approved out of 57 total applications). This approval rate is comparable to or higher than most other demographic groups in the dataset, including White non-Hispanic males (approximately 97-98%). The single denied application cannot establish a pattern of discrimination. While small sample sizes limit statistical power, the available evidence does not support a discrimination hypothesis for this group.

Analysis of the dataset shows 1,018 loan originations and 155 denials. For Hispanic or Latino White females in the 35-44 age group, the approval rate is approximately 92% (23 approvals out of 25 applications). This approval rate is consistent with or slightly above the overall dataset approval rate of ~87%. The applicant's demographic group does not show statistically meaningful evidence of discriminatory treatment in loan approval outcomes.

Analyzing loan outcomes for Hispanic or Latino White females aged 35-44: 11 loans originated, 2 denied (15.4% denial rate). Compared to the full dataset approval rate of ~93%, this group shows slightly elevated denial but the sample size is small (n=13). The denied applications had concerning financial metrics: one with >60% DTI and another with 50%-60% DTI, both exceeding standard lending thresholds. These denials appear driven by legitimate underwriting factors (debt-to-income ratios) rather than demographic discrimination. No clear pattern of disparate treatment based solely on ethnicity/race/sex is evident in the data.
